title: CRASH-092: http fopen request fulluri separate zval then ptr dtor frees shared context option uaf (use-after-free)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free at Zend/zend_execute_API.c:389 in _zval_ptr_dtor when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 09881626498d, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/http_fopen_wrapper.c:197-201 (free at :201). Claimed ":263" is the line number in the 2005 fix commit's tree, NOT in php-5.0.0.
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing. Needs: network: working loopback.

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the seam present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: the same image with the allocator seam retiring the payload at EVERY _efree, cache-absorbed or not, and re-deriving it under a fresh node when the cache hands the block to its next tenant: a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (php-real-object)

virtual-nested-exact.oracle: virtual-nested-pools with each payload bounded to the caller's request instead of REAL_SIZE(n): the arm that can see a defect inside PHP's own rounding slack (php-real-exact)

status: built 2026-10-27 from the corpus and our native oracle; what has run is in this record's arms (verdict, verdict_from) and under results/
note: population: asan-blind -- ASan reports it only with PHP's allocator patched (cache off, no 8-byte rounding); with zend_alloc.c as shipped the run reads OK. That is the selection, by measurement; which mechanism hides it, and which arm sees it, is what the arms record. Collected by the corpus as history-5x-stdext (historical-known, confidence high).
